title: BECE English Studies: Vocabulary & Register - NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies - Synonyms
subject: NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the bolded word:

After running a series of specialized tests, the doctor's **prognosis** for the critically injured patient was incredibly optimistic.
questions.explain: In a medical register, a 'prognosis' is the likely course or predicted outcome of a medical condition. Therefore, 'forecast' or prediction is the closest synonym.
questions.subject: NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the bolded word:

The unprecedented **influx** of refugees across the national border has heavily burdened the local healthcare systems.
questions.explain: An 'influx' refers to the arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things. Thus, 'arrival' is the closest synonym.
questions.subject: NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the bolded word:

During his nationwide broadcast, the President implored the citizens to remain absolutely **resolute** despite the harsh economic recession.
questions.explain: Being 'resolute' means being admirably purposeful, determined, and unwavering. 'Steadfast' carries the exact same meaning of firm and unwavering loyalty or determination.
questions.subject: NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the bolded word:

The psychiatrist noted that frequent abuse of hard synthetic substances can violently induce profound psychological **delusions** in users.
questions.explain: A 'delusion' is an idiosyncratic belief or impression maintained despite being completely contradicted by reality; in medical/drug abuse contexts, 'hallucinations' or severely false perceptions act as the closest synonym.
questions.subject: NECO BECE (Nigeria) English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the bolded word:

The ancestral colonial mansion, severely abandoned for decades, appeared incredibly **dilapidated** to the visiting structural inspectors.
questions.explain: In architectural or housing contexts, 'dilapidated' means existing in a state of disrepair or ruin, directly resulting from age or sheer neglect. 'Ruined' is the nearest appropriate synonym.
